question: Which statement best describes External stores?
options: getServerSnapshot is the optional third argument used during server-side rendering and the initial hydration render. It exists because the server has no browser APIs (no window, no navigator) and the server-rendered HTML must match what the client first produces. Omitting it when you do SSR throws an error; it should return a deterministic value both environments agree on.

getSnapshot returns the store's current value and is called on every render and after every notification. React compares the returned value by Object.is to decide whether to re-render, so it MUST return a referentially stable value when nothing changed. Returning a freshly allocated object or array each call makes React think the store always changed, producing an infinite render loop and the 'getSnapshot should be cached' warning.

An external store is any state container that lives outside React's own state model — a Redux/Zustand store, a browser API like navigator.onLine, or a hand-rolled object with getState/subscribe. It matters because React can't observe these sources through its normal render flow, so they need an explicit bridge. useSyncExternalStore is that bridge: it tells React how to read and how to be notified of changes.

subscribe is a function you pass to the Hook that receives a callback and must register it so the store invokes it on every change, returning an unsubscribe function for cleanup. React uses this to know exactly when to re-read the store. A critical gotcha: subscribe should be a stable reference (defined outside the component or memoized) — if it changes identity each render, React re-subscribes on every render, which is wasteful and can churn the store.

Tearing is a visual inconsistency where different parts of one render show different versions of the same external value, because the value mutated partway through an interruptible render. It only arises under concurrent rendering, where React can pause and resume mid-tree. useSyncExternalStore prevents it by reading synchronously and forcing a consistent re-render if the store changed during the render, so every consumer sees one value.

question: Which statement best describes getSnapshot?
options: Under concurrent features, React may begin a render, yield to the browser, and resume later. The Hook tracks the snapshot it rendered with and, before committing, checks whether the store moved on; if so it re-renders synchronously from the fresh value rather than committing stale data. This guarantee is exactly why the older useState + useEffect subscription pattern is unsafe in React 18+.

question: Which statement best describes getServerSnapshot?
options: Most developers never call useSyncExternalStore directly because libraries wrap it: react-redux, Zustand, Jotai, and Valtio all use it (or the useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector shim) for their React bindings. Knowing this clarifies when to use it yourself — for small custom stores or browser APIs — versus reaching for a library. The shim adds selector support so a component re-renders only when its selected slice changes.
